title: Workload-temporal batcher recommender and safe apply/rollback plan
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Build a recommendation engine that profiles temporal workload patterns (per-customer, per-route) and suggests continuous-batching parameters and cache hints. The system should surface safe apply actions that can be rolled back automatically if latency or correctness regressions are observed. Focus is on staged rollout logic, rollback thresholds, and heuristics that avoid harming tail-latency or model output quality.
acceptance_criteria: Collector can produce 7-day temporal histograms per route and per customer with bucket granularity of 5s and 1m
Recommender proposes a set of candidate batching configs (max_batch_tokens, max_batch_items, max_hold_ms, priority_weighting) for each route and rank by expected cost-savings and risk score
Console shows a one-click preview with estimated unit-cost delta and latency tail risk for each candidate
Safe-apply mechanism can execute a canary rollout to 1% traffic, measure SLOs for 30 minutes, and automatically rollback if any configured metric exceeds thresholds
Automated rollback triggers: 95th p95 latency increase > 15% or absolute p95 > route SLO OR generation-quality regression detected by prompt-level fidelity test suite
End-to-end integration tests for canary apply + rollback that run in CI and mock production metrics
implementation_notes: Profile inputs: sequence_length distribution, tokens_per_request, inter-arrival time distribution, route-level state (streaming vs non-streaming)
Key features: temporal windowing (sliding 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d), peak-detection, weekday/hour-of-day bucketing
Heuristic scoring: expected_tokens_saved = baseline_tokens_per_second - estimated_tokens_with_batching; risk_score = alpha * tail_latency_risk + beta * queue_depth_risk + gamma * cold_start_risk
Candidate parameters: max_hold_ms in [10, 200], max_batch_items in [2, 128], max_batch_tokens in [512, 65536], priority_weighting in [0.0-1.0]
Cold-start mitigation: prefer smaller max_hold_ms for newly active routes and enforce minimum throughput requirement before enabling large batch sizes
KV caching hinting: recommend prefix pinning for high-entropy session routes and TTL recommendations based on reuse rate
Safety: each change must include an instrumentation plan (cost delta probe, latency probe, quality probe) with baseline and canary windows
Data retention: profile data older than 90 days is aggregated and downsampled for trend analysis
decision_log: 2026-02-18: Chose temporal histogram approach over per-request heavy fingerprinting to reduce storage and compute overhead
2026-02-25: Agreed to prioritize p95 tail-latency risk in scoring function (alpha=0.6) after discussing customer SLAs
2026-03-03: Decided to use staged canaries (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with automated rollback; full rollout requires manual approval
2026-03-09: Opted to run fidelity checks using existing prompt suites instead of embedding-drift heuristics due to false positive rate
rollout_plan: Stage 0: dry-run recommender — generate candidate configs and surface to Console without applying
Stage 1: canary apply to internal traffic (1%) for 2 routes for 48 hours
Stage 2: external canary (1%) with automated 30-minute check windows; if stable, escalate to 10% for 2 hours
Stage 3: progressive ramp to 50% with continuous monitoring; final step requires SRE sign-off for 100%
Rollback: immediate reversion if any of the metric guards fire; rollback action is atomic config swap with verification hook
rollback_plan: Automatic triggers: p95 latency increase > 15% relative to baseline, error-rate spike > 0.5% absolute, fidelity test failures > 3
Manual override: on-call SRE or PM can force rollback via Console; change history and metrics snapshot are archived
Post-rollback: create a postmortem within 48 hours if rollback occurred during external canary
Fallback strategy: if full rollback fails to restore baseline, route traffic to fallback model variant (fallback model pinned in release)
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for score computation (risk and savings), seeded with synthetic traffic distributions
Integration test: canary apply flow with metric emulator that simulates increased tail latency
E2E QA: run on staging with real telemetry for 7 days and compare predicted vs observed cost-savings
Quality gates: fidelity test suite must pass at canary level before promotion
Load test: validate queue delay and memory usage under batched execution with 5x expected QPS

notes: Risk: over-aggressive batching can increase variance in latency and amplify queueing at peak; heuristics must penalize batch-hold for latency-sensitive routes
Opportunity: even moderate batching on long-tail text-completion routes could reduce token-unit cost by 12-25% for customers with bursty traffic
Implementation approach: split into phases — profiling, candidate generation, UI surface, safe-apply orchestration
Metrics to capture: tokens_saved, observed_unit_cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, model_error_rate, fidelity_regressions
